pictures.c: View of Montemurro after the 1857 earthquake (from Mallet [1862]).
Distribution of three orders of river terraces and of other erosional and depositional surfaces in the area between Montemurro and Grumento Nova (from Di Niro et al. [1992]).

Epicentral region of the 1857 earthquake also showing location and epicentral intensity of other historical earthquakes (from Benedetti et al. [1998]). The figure also reports the location of the Late-Quaternary Val d'Agri and Vallo di Diano Fault Systems according to Benedetti et al. [1998].

pictures.t: Map of the Agri fault system
pictures.c: Map of the Quaternary Val d'Agri SW-dipping normal-fault system identified from SPOT images, air photographs and fieldwork by Benedetti et al [1998]. According to these workers the system may have been activated in the 1857 earthquake.

Geological and topographic sections across Mt. Calvelluzzo, showing a 800 m-high and a 250 m-high escarpments interpreted by Benedetti et al. [1998] to be the effect of slip on a SW-dipping Val d'Agri fault system.

pictures.t: Regional structural section across the southern Apennines
pictures.c: Regional section across the Upper Agri Valley, suggesting also the absence of clearly detectable major normal faults (from Menardi-Noguera and Rea [2000]).

pictures.t: Uplift rate values in the Val d'Agri area
pictures.c: Distribution of uplift rate values in the Melandro and Upper Agri Valley (from Schiattarella et al. [2003]).
Morphostratigraphic sections of the Melandro and Upper Agri valleys (from Schiattarella et al. [2003]).

pictures.t: Geological and structural sketch of the high Agri river valley
pictures.c: Geologic sketch showing the main tecto-stratigraphic units forming the shoulders of the Upper Agri River Valley. Bold lines mark Quaternary normal faults responsible for the early stages of the basin opening and for the recent deformation (from Maschio et al. [2005]).

pictures.t: Geomorphological sketch of the Agri river valley and Monti della Maddalena range
pictures.c: Geomorphological scheme showing the presence of several young small basins perched on the crest of the Monti della Maddalena. Maschio et al. [2005] interpret these basins as the surface expression of a hidden NW-dipping seismogenic normal fault.

pictures.t: Topographic profiles across the Monti della Maddalena range
pictures.c: Topographic sections across the Monti della Maddalena and the Agri River valley, showing a characteristic hat-like topography due to the dissection of the crest of the mountain range (from Maschio et al. [2005]). The eastern shoulder of the valley displays a characteristic profile related to the presence of several splays of the SE-dipping fault system.

pictures.t: Longitudinal profiles along the Agri river
pictures.c: Longitudinal profiles showing variable behavior of the Agri River alongstream. This variability can be explained by differential vertical tectonic movements (from Maschio et al. [2005]).

pictures.t: Structural map of the high Agri river valley
pictures.c: Detailed structural map of the Monti della Maddalena range highlighting the presence of an array of NE-dipping normal faults forming the MMFS (from Maschio et al. [2005]).

pictures.t: Geologic cross-section across the Monti della Maddalena range and the Agri river valley
pictures.c: Geological cross-section showing the relationships between the NE-dipping Monti della Maddalena Fault System (MMFS) and the Eastern Agri Fault System (from Maschio et al. [2005]).

pictures.t: Quaternary faulting evolution of the Agri river valley
pictures.c: Reconstruction of the structural evolution of the upper Agri river basin according to Maschio et al. [2005]. The most recent stages of basin evolution are dominated by normal faulting along the NE-dipping Monti della Maddalena Fault System (MMFS).

pictures.t: Map of historical and instrumental seismicity of the southern Apennines
pictures.c: Map of historical and instrumental seismicity showing seismic sequenceS that occurred at the boundaries of the main historical earthquake epicentral areas (from Cucci et al. [2004]).

pictures.t: Focal plane solutions and breakout data
pictures.c: Fault plane solutions and breakout data highlighting a NE-SW oriented extensional regime (from Cucci et al. [2004]). The 1990 Potenza seismic sequence was caused by right-lateral faulting on E-W planes.

Epicenter relocations and fault plane solutions of the 1996 and 2002 seismic sequences (from Cucci et al. [2004]). The 1996 sequence occurred close to the southeastern termination of the 1857 seismogenic source, whereas the 2002 sequence bounds the Melandro-Pergola source to the NW.

pictures.t: Summary map of minimum horizontal stress orientation
pictures.c: Summary map of the minimum horizontal stress orientations derived from earthquake focal solutions and breakout data (from Cucci et al. [2004]).
